cards.text: Elihu, the man who's been answering Job and his friends, is STILL going. He says, "Bear with me a little longer, and I will show you that there is more to be said on God’s behalf." I get it, friend, because I say "just one more batch" too, and it is NEVER just one more batch.

cards.question: Elihu says he gets his knowledge from afar, and he's going to speak up for his Maker's ___.

cards.text: Elihu says his words are free of falsehood. Then he gets to his big point: God is mighty, mighty in strength of understanding.

cards.question: Elihu says God is so mighty that He looks down on the weak.

cards.text: Elihu says God doesn't keep the wicked alive, but He grants justice to the afflicted. And the righteous? God never takes His eyes off them.

cards.question: Elihu says God never takes His eyes off the righteous. Where does God put them?

answers.text: In the house of the LORD

cards.text: But say people end up bound in chains, caught in cords of affliction. Elihu says God tells them their deeds, and how arrogantly they've transgressed.

cards.question: When people are caught in cords of affliction, what does Elihu say God is doing?

answers.text: Leaving them to sort it out

cards.question: Elihu says that whether these people obey God or not, they'll end their days in prosperity.

cards.text: The godless in heart are different, Elihu says. Even when God binds them, they don't cry for help, and they die in their youth.

cards.question: Elihu says God rescues the afflicted. How does He do it?

cards.text: Now Elihu turns straight to Job. He says God drew Job from the jaws of distress to a spacious place, to a table full of richness.
But now, Elihu says, Job is laden with the judgment due the wicked. From a spacious place to a tight squeeze, and friend, I went from the counter to the back of a junk drawer, so I FEEL that one.

cards.question: Elihu warns Job not to let a large bribe lead him astray.
Elihu asks Job about his wealth and all his mighty effort. What's Elihu's point?

answers.text: They can't keep Job from distress
They prove God is still with Job
They should all go to the poor

cards.text: Elihu tells Job not to long for the night, when people vanish from their homes. Then he's got one more warning.

cards.question: Elihu warns Job to be careful not to turn to ___, which Elihu says Job has preferred to affliction.

cards.text: Now Elihu lifts his eyes higher. God is exalted in His power, he says, so who could appoint His way for Him, or tell Him He's done wrong?

cards.question: Elihu tells Job to remember to ___ God's work, the work men have praised in song.

cards.text: All mankind has seen it, Elihu says, and God is great beyond our knowledge, the number of His years unsearchable. Friend, I lost count of my years in ONE junk drawer.

cards.question: To show how great God is, Elihu starts with something from the sky. What is it?

cards.text: Then the storm rolls in: who can understand how the clouds spread out, or how the thunder roars from His pavilion? He scatters His lightning around Him and covers the depths of the sea.

cards.question: Elihu says that by these, God judges the nations and provides ___ in abundance.
Elihu says God's lightning just strikes wherever it happens to land.

cards.text: The thunder declares His presence, and even the cattle notice the rising storm. Elihu's own heart pounds and leaps from its place, and honestly, SAME, because when my oven door slams I hop a foot in the air, gold base and all.

cards.question: Elihu tells everyone to listen closely to the thunder. What does he say the thunder is?

cards.text: God unleashes His lightning to the ends of the earth, then thunders with His majestic voice. He does great things we cannot comprehend, Elihu says.

cards.question: Elihu says God tells the gentle rain to stay light and gentle.
Elihu says God seals up the hand of every man. What reason does Elihu give?

answers.text: So all men may know His work
So no one can fight back

cards.text: Even the wild animals head into their dens and settle down, as the tempest comes and the cold blows in from the north. Smart animals, because when it's cold out, NOBODY is getting me away from my warm oven.

cards.question: Elihu says the ice forms and the watery expanses freeze by God's ___.

cards.text: He loads the clouds with moisture and scatters His lightning through them. The clouds swirl about at His direction, doing all He commands over the face of all the earth.

cards.question: Whether the storm comes for punishment or for His land, what does Elihu say God does it in?

cards.text: Then Elihu calls Job by name: "Listen to this, O Job; stand still and consider the wonders of God."

cards.question: Elihu asks Job if he knows how God dispatches the clouds or makes the lightning flash. What's Elihu getting at?

answers.text: Job should learn to read the sky
Job brought on the storm himself

cards.text: Elihu even mentions Job's clothes getting hot when the south wind hushes the land. Friend, that's me by the oven in a full apron: sweaty, and in charge of absolutely NOTHING.

cards.question: Elihu asks Job if he can spread out the skies like God, as strong as a mirror of bronze.
Elihu asks Job to teach them what to say to God. Why does Elihu say they can't draw up their case?

cards.text: Then Elihu wonders if God should be told he wants to speak, because who would ask to be swallowed up? That's the boss asking who wants to present at the big meeting, and every arm in the room stays DOWN.
Now Elihu paints one more picture. After the wind sweeps the skies clean, nobody can stare at the bright sun.

cards.question: Elihu says God comes out of the north in golden splendor, and awesome ___ surrounds Him.

cards.text: The Almighty is beyond our reach, Elihu says. "He is exalted in power!"

cards.question: Elihu says that in His justice and great righteousness, God does not ___.
Elihu wraps up by saying men fear God. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He is not partial to the wise in heart
He keeps His plans a secret from all

cards.text: And that's Elihu's last word for now. But friend, the book of Job isn't finished yet, so keep that oven warm.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "just one more batch", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says Elihu is 'the man who's been answering Job and his friends.' That fact comes from outside the passage (Job 32:1-6), but the card cites only Job 36:1-2.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'Whether these people obey God or not' uses 'these people' to point back to people described on earlier cards that are no longer on screen. The question doesn't say who they are, which is people caught in cords of affliction (Job 36:8).

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The core action in Job 36:17 is Job being laden with the judgment due the wicked. The joke compares it to being moved from the counter to a junk drawer, which is a different action. It also reframes the verse as 'From a spacious place to a tight squeeze,' blending the comparison into the Bible setting. 'Tight squeeze' isn't in the text.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'Elihu says that by these, God judges the nations' uses 'these' to point back to the clouds, thunder and lightning from an earlier card the baker can't see. The question never says what 'these' are.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The card carries three moments of the passage (the thunder declares His presence, the cattle notice the storm, Elihu's heart pounds) plus a joke, all in one long second sentence.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: 'Elihu tells everyone to listen closely' names an audience that Job 37:2 leaves open. The question also never names God, so 'His voice', 'His footsteps' and 'His chariots' have no stated subject.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin runs his own ovens, so 'by the oven... in charge of absolutely NOTHING' contradicts itself and doesn't click. The core action of Job 37:17 is feeling the heat of the south wind. Being in charge of nothing doesn't match it.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'He is not partial to the wise in heart,' uses biblical phrasing. The wrong answers ('He keeps His plans a secret from all', 'He punishes every single mistake') sound plain and modern, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: 'That's Elihu's last word for now' implies Elihu will speak again. In Job, Elihu never speaks again: the LORD answers Job next (Job 38:1).

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse. It still cites Job 37:24, which the choice card before it already covers.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the 'story continues' line, what should its 'verses' field cite: the passage's last verse, the stop's range, or nothing?
